text.en:
On Pongal morning Meena's family cooked sweet rice in a new pot in the yard. Her friend Imran came with sweets for them.
A month later, Meena's family went to Imran's house for Eid.
"Our festivals are different but our joy is the same," said Imran.

India has many festivals: Pongal, Diwali, Eid, Christmas, Onam, Holi, Baisakhi and Gurpurab. Many are linked to seasons, harvests, or great events in the lives of religious teachers.
Festivals bring families and neighbours together. People share food, wear new clothes, decorate homes and sing and dance.
Traditions such as folk dances, music and crafts are passed from older people to children. This is how our culture lives on.
India has many festivals like Pongal, Diwali, Eid and Christmas.
Some festivals welcome the harvest. Others remember great people and events.
People share food and joy, and neighbours join each other's festivals.
Traditions are passed on from elders to children.

problem.en: Why is Pongal celebrated in Tamil Nadu in January?

text.en: It is the harvest festival after the crops are cut.
People cook new rice and thank the Sun and cattle.
So Pongal is a festival of the harvest.

prompt.en: A friend says festivals are only for one community. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: Many festivals are enjoyed by neighbours of all communities.

points.en: Some mark harvests or great events.
Festivals and traditions bring people together.
